title: Matmul performance analysis (summary)
description:
Summary of PERF_ANALYSIS.md for the 16×16 int8 weight-stationary systolic array at 90 MHz on the DE1-SoC. Full write-up in the matmul-accel repo (link above).

Main conclusion: performance is bound by the software tiling scheme. Each matmul the hardware runs multiplies a tk×tn slab of W by a tn×tm slab of X into a tk×tm output patch. A bigger output patch gets more MACs from each byte sent over the bridge (density), so the same problem needs fewer matmuls and fewer bytes.

- A 256×256 matmul tiled into 128×128 output tiles runs at the same speed as a single 128×128 matmul: same tile shape, density and utilization. Tiling it as one 256×256 output (W in 256×64 strips, X in 64×256 strips) halves the matmul count and roughly doubles throughput.
- A 128×128 matmul is capped at 64 MAC/B because a tile cannot be larger than the matrix. 256×256 reaches 128 MAC/B, the limit set by the 64 KB output canvas, so 512×512 plateaus at the same density.
- Peak compute is 46.1 GOP/s (2 ops × 256 PEs × 90 MHz). Best measured compute-only throughput is 40.15 GOP/s, about 87% of peak.
- The gap comes from 16 head and 16 tail cycles per weight block: utilization = tm / (tm + 32), 80% at tm = 128 and 88.9% at tm = 256. Overlapping the next block's head with the previous block's tail would bring utilization close to 100%; that needs the output path to hold two blocks in flight.
